name: Probability for Computer Science / Імовірність для комп'ютерних наук
ai_policy: AI allowed like any online source, but any use for homework must be cited. Homework is defended in person: the student must be able to explain every step.
assessment: HW 1-4: 10 points each, due weeks 5, 8, 11, 14; up to 5 days late at -10%/day; defended in person
Midterm (week 8, written, one handwritten A4 summary sheet allowed): 30
Final (week 15, written, one handwritten A4 summary sheet allowed): 30
Extra points: up to 10; course total capped at 100
notes: Teacher's lectures are weak for this student: teach from the approved books — Blitzstein & Hwang 'Introduction to Probability' (probabilitybook.net), Stanford CS109 lectures, Grinstead & Snell — plus the course's Moodle files.

topics.title: Sample spaces, events, operations on events, finite and countable models
Axioms of probability, probability space, sigma-algebra, geometric probability
Total probability theorem and Bayes' theorem
Discrete random variables: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, Poisson, hypergeometric
Expectation and variance of discrete RVs, probability generating functions
Poisson limit theorem, local and integral De Moivre–Laplace theorems
Joint discrete distributions, independence of RVs, covariance, correlation
Continuous RVs: CDF, PDF; uniform, exponential, normal, gamma
Expectation and variance of continuous RVs; distributions of functions of RVs
Multivariate continuous distributions, marginals, independence, covariance
Chebyshev's inequality, 3-sigma rule, Law of Large Numbers, Central Limit Theorem
Stochastic processes: Poisson process, Wiener process
